newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt mixed ahead of US data, focus on Russia.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt mixed ahead of US data, focus on Russia.

text.p: Brady bonds were mixed on Thursday ahead of U.S. data though Russia continued to grab the spotlight on Wednesday's news it had reconciled 60 percent of its debt with the London Club, traders said.
"It's good to see the number coming up and off the back of that people are feeling more confident," said one trader at a major U.S. bank in London.
Russia has to fully reconcile 90 percent of the $24 billion principal of its total $35 billion owed to commercial bank creditors in order for the debt restructuring deal to be finalized.
Russian debt, which soared to new record levels on Wednesday on the news, was unchanged to slightly lower with the rest of the market.
But market experts said potential for further gains had increased on expectations that the closing of the debt restructuring was drawing near.
They said the publishing of weekly reports of fully reconciled debt volumes set to begin in August was also a positive sign towards greater transparency.

"I think the real development is that they (Russian Finance Ministry) will have weekly status reports from next month so we will have a far clearer indication of just how they are progressing," said Neil Lockwood, senior emerging market economist at ANZ Investment.

Vietnam, which is also in the process of reconciling its loans with the London Club of creditors, has also attracted investor interest in recent weeks on renewed prospects that it will close its debt restructuring plan by mid-September or early October.

Though Vietnamese debt had sharply lagged the rest of the Brady market on previous concerns about its debt restructuring package, market experts said spreads should narrow dramatically on renewed hopes the deal will close in coming months.
"Vietnam has lagged a long way behind the average Brady spread so it's a long way behind and it does have a quite a lot of scope to catch up and interest does seem to be escalating," said Lockwood.

In the broader emerging debt market, participants decided to keep to the sidelines as they awaited the U.S. second quarter GDP report due out on Thursday and the July unemployment report due out on Friday.
"As far as I am aware, there is very little going on. After yesterday's strength, London trading is taking a bit of a breather," said another trader. --Diane Craft, London Newsroon +44 171 542 5110
